newsitem.title: USA: Reuters surveys U.S. brokers, fund managers.
newsitem.headline: Reuters surveys U.S. brokers, fund managers.

text.p: Reuters Holdings Plc Wednesday inaugurated a U.S. version of its annual surveys of equity markets, gathering data from the largest corporations, fund management companies and securities houses and pointing up differences in the way each group views the others.

"What we see here is a more advanced form of what we see in other parts of the world," said Stephen Parker, managing director of Tempest Consultants Inc, which was commissioned by Reuters to conduct the research.

In an interview, Parker said while U.S. brokers are enjoying the fruits of a bull market at the moment with mergers and acquisition activity booming and bigger bonuses, the truth is that "the long term situation is declining profitabilty." While profits might be setting records, he said, "the actual ratios are getting much tougher, the margins are under pressure."

Parker said the squeeze on margins has helped produce a wave of merger activity among financial service firms. He said another response of the U.S. firms has been to look to faster-growing overseas markets for expansion.

Among the fund managers, the survey found that 16.05 percent say they are spending less time reading and listening to broker research while only 3.70 percent say they are spending more time with the broker research. The biggest group, 80.25 percent, is spending the same amount of time with broker research.

Asked if they plan to beef up in-house research capabilities over the next 12 months, 51.85 percent of the fund managers said such an increase is planned. Less than half, 46.91 percent, said they planned to have about the same amount of in-house research, and only 1.23 percent said they planned to reduce in-house resources.

Parker noted that the survey of fund managers was weighted according to the amount of investment money represented by each firm. "We are not playing a 'one-man-one vote' game," he said. "We are capturing the weight of money, the business reality."
The survey uncovered a discrepancy between the way corporations amd analysts view the response of the corporations to a recommendation to sell a stock.

More than three-quarters, 75.66 percent, of the corporations said one of their responses would be to increase communication and extend access to the analyst. But 62.65 percent of the analysts said the corporation would reduce communication and reduce access.
"There's a big problem there," Parker said of the survey results on the reponse to a sell recommendation. "The two sides are not being honest with each other."
The survey concluded there is a widening gulf between the fund managers and brokers, in part due to the interest of the fund managers in seeking the best price for a transaction.

The survey ranked analysts and securities firms in various categories. The corporations provided the data for one set of rankings while the fund managers were the input for a second ranking in most of the categories.
At a luncheon in New York, awards were presented to five firms, one individual and one research team based on the rankings of research and service.

Goldman, Sachs & Co came away with four awards, for best securities house for execution as voted by fund management groups; for best securities house for sales, as voted by fund management groups; as best securities house for research, as voted by fund management groups and best securities house for research as voted by the corporations.

John Avery of Fidelity Investments received the award for best indivdiual manager according to the corporations. The Capital Group was voted best fund management group by the corporations. The insurance research team at Sanford C. Bernstein Co received the award for having the best securities house industry sector team.
The full report, running more than 200 pages, is titled "The 1997 Reuters Survey of U.S. Larger Company Investment Research, Sales & Trading."
The event in New York was sponsored by Reuters America Inc, which is the primary American operating division of Reuters Holdings plc.
